title: Finite locally constant etale module sheaves descend along affine inverse limits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set, let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ with projections $p_i:X\to X_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose $F$ is finite locally constant as a module sheaf: there is an etale covering $\{U_a\to X\}$ on which $F|_{U_a}\cong\underline{M_a}$ for finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_a$ [def-constructible-locally-constant, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then there exist $i\in I$, a sheaf $F_i$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $(X_i)_{\mathrm{et}}$ which is etale locally constant with finite $\Lambda$-module values in this same sense, and an isomorphism $p_i^{-1}F_i\cong F$ of $\Lambda$-module sheaves, where inverse image has its canonical constant-coefficient module structure [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. No Noetherian hypothesis on the schemes is imposed.

proof.text: Each projection $p_i$ is affine. Since $I$ is nonempty, choose one stage; an affine morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so the qcqs permanence statements show that $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The one-stratum partition $X=X$ and the given finite constant local models witness constructibility of $F$ in the finite-value module sense. Apply constructible-module limit descent to obtain $i$, a constructible module sheaf $F_i$ on $X_i$, and a module isomorphism $p_i^{-1}F_i\cong F$. This only supplies a constructible model; it does not yet supply local constancy at a stage.

Choose a finite affine open cover $(W_b)_{b\in B}$ of $X_i$. For each $b$, its pullback $W_{b,X}=W_b\times_{X_i}X$ is affine, since it is affine over the affine scheme $W_b$. Pull the given trivializing etale cover back to $W_{b,X}$ and use finite affine etale refinement there. We obtain finitely many affine etale maps $U_{b,a}\to W_{b,X}$ covering $W_{b,X}$, and finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_{b,a}$ with $F|_{U_{b,a}}\cong\underline{M_{b,a}}$. A refined member factors through a given trivializing member, so the trivialization restricts; inverse image of a constant module sheaf is constant. All these comparisons preserve scalars by the constant-coefficient module inverse-image lemma. Only finitely many pairs $(b,a)$ occur. No assertion that an intersection of arbitrary affine opens is affine is used.

For each $b$, apply finite affine covering descent with fixed affine etale target $W_b$ over $X_i$ and the finite covering $U_{b,a}\to p_i^*W_b$. In its auxiliary-factorization slots take every $U_q$ to be the terminal etale object $X_i$ and the unique structure arrow. It gives a stage $j_b\ge i$ and affine etale objects $U_{j_b,b,a}$ covering $W_b\times_{X_i}X_{j_b}$, whose pullbacks to $X$ are the prescribed $U_{b,a}$ over $W_{b,X}$. Directedness gives a common $j\ge j_b$ for the finitely many $b$. Pull these covers to $X_j$; the affine etale base-change system preserves standard covering families. Their targets $W_{b,j}$ form the inverse-image open cover of $X_j$, so the combined family $(U_{j,b,a}\to X_j)_{b,a}$ is an etale cover. Put $F_j=t_{ji}^{-1}F_i$.

source.place: Tag 0GL2, finite trivializing cover descent, using Tag 0EYL (lemma-colimit-affine-sites)

proof.text: For each pair $(b,a)$ let $B_{b,a}=F_j|_{U_{j,b,a}}$ and $C_{b,a}=\underline{M_{b,a}}$ on $U_{j,b,a}$. The constructibility comparison with the coefficient-category predicate, followed by constructible pullback and the comparison back, shows that $B_{b,a}$ is constructible in the same finite-value module sense as $F_i$. The constant finite module sheaf $C_{b,a}$ is constructible by its one-stratum constant trivialization. For $k\ge j$ put $U_{k,b,a}=U_{j,b,a}\times_{X_j}X_k$. The scheme-over-limit lemma identifies their inverse limit with $U_{b,a}$. Their transitions are affine and every $U_{k,b,a}$ is affine, hence qcqs. Constant pullback and module inverse-image composition identify the pullbacks of $B_{b,a},C_{b,a}$ to $U_{b,a}$ with $F|_{U_{b,a}},\underline{M_{b,a}}$. The chosen trivialization therefore gives a module isomorphism $\alpha_{b,a}$ between those pullbacks.

Apply clause (1) of constructible-module morphism descent to $\alpha_{b,a}$ and to its inverse, on the system $(U_{k,b,a})_{k\ge j}$. They descend, possibly at different indices, to morphisms $u_{b,a}:B_{b,a,k}\to C_{b,a,k}$ and $v_{b,a}:C_{b,a,k}\to B_{b,a,k}$. Take a common upper bound for these indices for every one of the finitely many pairs and pull all maps there. Their pullbacks remain $\alpha_{b,a}$ and $\alpha_{b,a}^{-1}$, using the module inverse-image composition comparisons. At this point no claim that the descended maps are isomorphisms has been made.

On each limit $U_{b,a}$, the pullbacks of $v_{b,a}\circ u_{b,a}$ and $\mathrm{id}_{B_{b,a,k}}$ are equal, and those of $u_{b,a}\circ v_{b,a}$ and $\mathrm{id}_{C_{b,a,k}}$ are equal: they are respectively $\alpha_{b,a}^{-1}\alpha_{b,a}=1$ and $\alpha_{b,a}\alpha_{b,a}^{-1}=1$. Clause (2) of constructible-module morphism descent detects each of these two equalities at a later stage. Constructibility at later stages follows again by constructible pullback and the module constructibility comparison. A common upper bound $l$ of the finitely many equality stages makes both identities hold for every pair. Functors preserve identities and composition, so the identities persist at $l$. Thus $F_l|_{U_{l,b,a}}\cong\underline{M_{b,a}}$ as module sheaves for every pair, not merely as sheaves of sets.

The base-changed family $(U_{l,b,a}\to X_l)_{b,a}$ still covers, by covering preservation of affine etale base change. The isomorphisms just constructed with the finite modules $M_{b,a}$ are exactly finite local constancy in the statement. Furthermore $F_l=t_{li}^{-1}F_i$, so module inverse-image composition and the isomorphism in Step 1 give $p_l^{-1}F_l\cong p_i^{-1}F_i\cong F$. No compatibility between different local trivializations is required: $F_l$ already exists globally, and these isomorphisms certify a local property of it. This concludes with the original finite ring and without any Noetherian assumption on the schemes.
